
### FELLA

FELLA requires KEGG IDs of significantly regulated metabolites. It uses a holistic graph
representation of the KEGG database instead of the classical over representation
analysis to find perturbed pathways.

Starting point is the data frame with unique KEGG IDs. The unique compounds data
frame from the KEGG code block above will be searched according to your input in the shiny app.

```{r Extract KEGG IDs of regulated compounds for FELLA analysis,echo=FALSE, results='markup', tidy=TRUE}
# use xlfile.KEGG.unique for FELLA

# Loop through each Log2 Fold Change column
for (i in seq_along(log_cols)) {
  log_col <- log_cols[i]        # Current Log2 Fold Change column
  pval_col <- pval_cols[i]        # Corresponding p-value column
  
  print(log_col)
  print(pval_col)
  
  # Filter the dataframe based on the conditions
  filtered_df <- xlfile.KEGG.unique %>%
      filter(
        (!!sym(log_col) >= log2FC ) |
        (!!sym(log_col) <= -log2FC) |
        ((!!sym(pval_col) <= pvalue) & (!!sym(log_col) >= log2FCpV)) |
        ((!!sym(pval_col) <= pvalue) & (!!sym(log_col) <= -log2FCpV))
        ) %>%
    select(KEGG, !!sym(log_col), !!sym(pval_col))
  
  output_file_name <- format_output_filename(log_col)
  output_file_name_txt <- paste0(output_file_name, ".txt") 
  
  # Construct the full path with the FELLA directory
  output_file_path <- file.path(FELLA, paste0(user,"_FELLA_", output_file_name_txt)) 
  
  cat("###START###\n")
  cat("Nr. of rows FELLA:", output_file_name, nrow(filtered_df))
  cat("\n###END###\n")
  
  # Write only the KEGG column to a text file in the FELLA directory
  write.table(filtered_df$KEGG, file = output_file_path, sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
}
```
